thread.title: Zim Mover Investigation
thread.preview:
I read the full earlier report and completed the follow-up. **The new evidence provides better record locators, but still does not identify the Manhattan customer, address, assigned crew, vehicle or completed delivery.**

[Full follow-up report — 17 pages](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_2f6c21f4765c819196b9acd8f6e5212c&account_id=personal)

### Strongest new leads

| Lead | What the records establish—and leave unresolved |
|---|---|
| **Item 32’s physical evidence package** | A bag photograph identifies **two notebooks from a teal satchel, numbered 32**. The inventory places Item 32 within **1B4 / E01889578**, a bundle containing multiple items. This improves the custody cross-reference; the actual attendance entries and their owners remain unidentified. **FBI section 6, PDF p. 9; section 1, pp. 7, 107.** :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"} |
| **Proposed “Sub-file V”** | A **September 21, 2001 memo** requests a file for copies of the van inventory. This supplies a specific target for Items 1, 2 and 32, but does not prove that the file was created, completed or retained. **Section 5, p. 16.** :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"} |
| **Williamsport’s 13-page fax package** | A September 19 enclosure list names a **Penske lease and Pennsylvania traffic citation**; the adjacent fax cover specifies 13 pages. These could establish vehicle and driver identities. **The bill of lading is not explicitly listed**, and the fax’s conflicting date markings remain unresolved. **Section 3, pp. 40–42.** :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"} |
| **Previously overlooked Hoboken pickup** | A November interview describes a **September 11 steel-rod pickup at a storage facility**, plus unavailable computerized work schedules. Redactions prevent identifying the participants, customer or carrier. No connection to the Manhattan shipment is established. **NY Serial 337, PDF pp. 4–5.** :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"} |

The report also documents an ordinary commercial alternative: contemporaneous Boxesnstuff advertising offered **UPS/FedEx shipping**. That establishes advertised shipping options, not the carrier used for this shipment.

**Your actual sent November 9 supplement already names all four requested follow-up targets.** I verified an automatic acknowledgment, but no substantive confirmation of accepted search scope. The new findings mainly sharpen those existing locators.

The report includes the **42-day, five-person table**, 32 unassigned activity entries, detailed source notes, negative searches and request comparison. No reviewed job record could safely populate the five men’s named assignments; Pennsylvania accounts remain separate. Those gaps do not establish that no work occurred.

No WTC/Zim job was established, and a job or badge alone would not establish an explosives role. No contacts or requests were made.

content.text:
do a follow up and deep reseach on new leads. consider: The chat’s response lists seven principal leads, but it says the [full report](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_fc2e5fb912248191abdddf88b318cc0b\&account_id=personal) contains a fuller chronology and negative-search log. I haven’t yet examined that full report, so I can’t say whether those seven are everything it found.

**Yes, a focused follow-up is worthwhile**, especially on the Manhattan delivery. I’d ask Scooby to:

1. Re-examine the original interview and related FBI pages for the delivery’s **customer, address, assigned workers, vehicle and eventual disposition**.
2. Locate the actual **Item 32 attendance pages, route 31 dispatch and bill of lading**, including duplicates or more complete releases, and determine which people and dates they cover.
3. Build a **day-by-day table for the five New Jersey detainees**, keeping the separately detained Pennsylvania movers distinct and marking days with no reliable assignment.
4. Compare the precise records with our **submitted requests**, so we can tell whether another search lead would add anything.

The Manhattan account is worth tracing because it names a destination and a delivery due immediately before September 11. Its significance is still unknown: the summary identifies no address, completed delivery or WTC connection. I haven’t sent a follow-up.

content.text: Please conduct deep research into where Urban Moving Systems (UMS), Max Movers and their personnel claimed to have been working during the weeks before September 11, 2001. Build a dated, source-by-source job and personnel chronology for August 1–September 11, extending where useful to late July. Find original FBI FD-302s and employee/employer statements, customer interviews, bills of lading, invoices, schedules, dispatch and delivery records, vehicle assignments, tolls, receipts, insurance certificates, access/entry records and contemporaneous corporate filings. Identify exact date, location, client (only where properly supported), company, worker or crew, vehicle, activity, who reported it, and the original document/page; mark missing dates, redactions, attribution and identity crosswalks. Investigate the reported September 10 Doric apartment move, separately reported Ohio and Illinois deliveries, and any other jobs, but do not assume the two Philadelphia detainees were among the five New Jersey detainees or that a location and job belong to the same person. Look for records that confirm and contradict the claims, gaps and incompatible times, ordinary jobs and work at the World Trade Center or for Zim, while not assuming such a job exists. Distinguish employee claims, third-party verification, administrative documents and retrospective summaries; avoid counting copies as independent corroboration, and do not infer intelligence affiliation, foreknowledge, explosives or coordination from a moving job alone. Supply direct source links and page numbers, a clear negative-search log and a prioritized list of missing dispatch/access/custody records, plus relevant requests already described in project sources only when verified. Do not contact anyone, submit requests, or send messages. Provide a concise findings table and detailed source notes.

items.text:
**The clearest records support ordinary moving activity, including FBI-reported customer confirmations in Ohio and Illinois. They do not provide a complete August dispatch history or establish a WTC/Zim job.**

The full chronology, detailed source notes, negative-search log and prioritized record targets are in [:chatgpt-content-reference{index="10"}](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_fc2e5fb912248191abdddf88b318cc0b&account_id=personal).

### Principal findings

Page numbers below refer to the original PDFs.

| Activity date | Finding | Evidence and locator |
|---|---|---|
| **Aug. 17, Aug. 24, Sept. 6** | Hoboken fuel purchases associated with UMS van **JRJ13Y**. No named driver or customer. | FBI transcriptions of receipts: **Section 3, p. 54**, Item 42(7). :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"} |
| **Aug. 21, 12:35 p.m.** | ADT salesperson reported surveying a Bayonne warehouse after meeting two unidentified men associated with UMS. | NJSP memo: **Section 3, pp. 31–32**. Proposed security work—not a confirmed customer move or completed installation. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"} |
| **About Aug. 27** | A UMS worker reportedly recruited another man to help deliver furniture to **Arkansas**. | **Philadelphia Serial 357, p. 2**. Invitation documented; completion, customer, city and vehicle unconfirmed. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"} |
| **Sept. 10** | **Doric-associated apartment move:** three movers and a white box truck with red cab. The witness said **none of the five photographs depicted the movers**. | **Section 1, pp. 71–74**; interviews Sept. 12, transcribed Sept. 14. Elevator-request messages and a liability certificate reportedly supplied to FBI provide concrete record leads. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"} |
| **Sept. 10–11** | Penske loaded at UMS; deliveries to **Worthington, Ohio**, and **Evanston, Illinois**. FBI reported contacting customers who confirmed deliveries, alongside toll-receipt evidence. | **PH Serial 357, p. 3; Serial 2, pp. 2–3.** These concern the **two Pennsylvania detainees**, separately from the five New Jersey detainees. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"} |
| **Trip dates unstated** | Employer-side **route 31** assignment: Marietta → St. Louis → Nashua pickup → Lawrence delivery. | **Section 5, p. 39**; interview Sept. 13. Assigned itinerary, without verified completed stops or a reliable vehicle/customer crosswalk. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="5"} |
| **Due Sept. 10; packing Sept. 11** | Employee described boxes being prepared for an overdue **Manhattan delivery**. | **Section 5, pp. 21–22**. No client, address, completed delivery or WTC connection identified. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="6"} |

### Most consequential unresolved records

The strongest targets are **Item 32’s apparent August–September attendance pages**, **route 31’s dispatch record**, the **UMS bill of lading shown during the September 12 interview**, and the **Doric certificate fax/1A attachments**. These are records expressly described in the releases. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="7"}

The report preserves conflicts—including **10:25 versus 11:30 p.m.** for the initial Pennsylvania stop and differing employer/worker itineraries—without forcing a reconciliation. It also separates the August 10 insurance fax from job evidence: that fax identifies two carriers in an insurance exchange, not a WTC assignment. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="8"}

No complete dispatch ledger, attributable WTC entry event or Zim transaction was located. That is a bounded search result, not proof of absence. No contacts or requests were made; nothing found establishes an explosives role.

content.text: Please conduct focused deep research on the 2001 Zim relocation and World Trade Center access records. Identify likely present custodians of Zim and Hunter Management relocation procurement and payment files, move approvals, loading-dock and elevator bookings, visitor-card issuance records and access-event logs. Search for public vendor awards or contemporaneous records identifying any actual moving company or subcontractor, not only Urban Moving Systems or Max Movers. Distinguish occupant rosters from actual event logs, confirm custody and retention only where supported, and provide original source links and exact page or document locators. Report negative findings and competing explanations. A moving job or badge alone would not establish an explosives role. Do not contact anyone or send requests.

items.text:
**I found no public record identifying Zim’s physical mover or subcontractor.** Searches beyond UMS and Max produced no verified vendor award, paid invoice, bill of lading, or Zim-specific dock/elevator entry.

### Strongest custodian leads

| Records sought | Best-supported lead and limitation |
|---|---|
| **Zim procurement and payments** | **ZIM American Integrated Shipping Services Company, LLC**, 4425 Zim Way, Virginia Beach—accounting, procurement, facilities and legal archives. The 2025 Form 20-F identifies the entity/address at **printed p.45**; retention of 2001 files is unconfirmed. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"} |
| **Hunter move-management files** | Historical **Hunter Management** project records and James Pirot’s project trail. I found no verified successor or archive-transfer instrument; his current firm is a person locator, not a confirmed archive recipient. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"} |
| **Move approvals, dock/elevator bookings and visitor records** | **PA/Silverstein transition archives**, with **ABM operating/litigation files** as an additional elevator lead. Reiss’s testimony, **pp.3 and 8**, documents overlapping transition responsibilities. No requested operational log was located. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"} |
| **Confirmed cataloged holdings** | **Library of Virginia:** Zim incentive-project file, accession **40168**, Series II, **Box 2/Folder 15**. **New York Historical:** July 2001 building lease, **MS3128**, Series IV, **Box 5/Folder 12**. Contents remain uninspected. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"} |

**The strongest new access lead:** in **May 2004**, NYC DOHMH supplied RTI with a PA list of **95,442 badge holders**. The manual, **printed p.25/PDF p.35**, documents that transfer—not individual entry events, temporary-visitor coverage, or present retention. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}

NIST separately documents lost **construction and maintenance logs** for WTC 1, 2 and 7, **printed p.48/PDF p.100**. That finding cannot be extended to every access record or tenant/vendor duplicate. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="5"}

The seven-page report includes exact links, succession evidence, the ABM exhibit trail, security-contractor leads, negative searches and competing explanations:

[:chatgpt-content-reference{index="7"}](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_339d369c534881918c6140d42a162890&account_id=personal)

No contacts or requests were made. A moving job or badge alone would not establish an explosives role.

content.text:
Yes. I’d send **two focused follow-ups**: one on the visitor card and one on evidence custody and the limits of the Newark finding. Both have specific records to trace and could produce evidence that either strengthens or weakens the theory.

The six earlier research prompts were already sent and answered, according to the [follow-up record](/Users/admin/.codex/worktrees/13ee/911/research/ums-wtc-theory-2026-11-05/assessment-and-hq-record-search-2026-11-06/RESEARCH-AND-FOLLOWUPS.md). These would build on the subsequent source checks rather than repeat those searches.

1. **Visitor card and a possible WTC job** — follow up in the [Zim Mover Investigation chat](https://chatgpt.com/c/6aed5cff-530c-83ea-8190-98115bea8f5d):
   > Trace the WTC visitor card listed in the September 11 FBI property receipt, section 2 PDF p. 81, and the East Rutherford officer’s report on pp. 72–73. Find clearer or less-redacted versions, the referenced receipt attachment, evidence crosswalk, card image, holder, issuer, date, host and any entry records. Test whether the receipt can be reliably connected to the driver’s bag, and whether the card connects to a UMS or Max job, including Zim. Examine other holders and ordinary personal or commercial visits as alternatives. Search for positive and negative FBI comparisons and identify surviving custody and records. Give source links and page numbers, and distinguish a documented match from an inference. Do not contact anyone or submit requests.
   This is the strongest new lead because the police report supplies a possible connection between the van driver’s bag and the receipt. The [local review](/Users/admin/.codex/worktrees/13ee/911/research/ums-wtc-theory-2026-11-05/wtc-visitor-card-trace-2026-11-06/REVIEW.md) also explains why the holder, building, actual visit and any moving job remain unconfirmed.

Continue the Zim mover search using the dated Port Authority listing for 1 WTC floor 16 suite 1601 and Hunter Management's reported owner's-representative role as locators. Find Zim vendor selection and paid invoices, Hunter move-management records, bills of lading, subcontractor and insurance records, and building dock, freight-elevator and access logs. Include records identifying another carrier and any negative search. Compare the August 10, 2001 UMS/Max insurance fax and the FBI interview's NK1765 / 1A attachment without assuming either establishes a Zim job. Provide dated provenance, actual access and identity evidence; a move is not evidence of explosive installation. Do not contact custodians.
